title: Tale of the Dethroned Ruler (മലയാളം)

full_text:
A powerful King of Persia was deposed in a military coup and forced to flee his capital in disguise. Having escaped with his life, he purchased a small, secluded orchard of apricot and olive trees in a distant province, earning his bread by his own manual labor.

For ten years, he pruned his trees, channeled mountain spring water to the roots, harvested the fruit, and sold it in the local village market.

One afternoon, an old courtier who had served in his former palace passed through the orchard and recognized the former monarch, dressed in a coarse linen tunic and wooden clogs.

The courtier wept with pity: 'Alas, my royal master! What a tragic fate! You who once sat upon a golden throne and commanded armies now shovel earth around apricot trees!'

The former king smiled with radiant serenity, wiped the sweat from his brow, and offered his old courtier a basket of sweet, ripe apricots:

'Do not weep for me, old friend! When I wore that golden crown, I slept with a naked sword beneath my pillow, terrified of assassins; every courtier was a flatterer, every feast was poisoned by suspicion, and my soul was a prisoner of anxiety.

Today, my bread is earned with clean hands; my sleep is as sweet as childhood, the birds in my trees sing without flattery, and my heart knows peace.

I did not lose a kingdom; I was delivered from a gilded prison to become the sovereign of my own soul.'
moral: The true kingdom is peace of soul; earthly crowns bring anxiety, while honest labor brings sweet sleep. [ML]
